definition: In computer vision, a stixel (portmanteau of "stick" and "pixel") is a superpixel representation of depth information in an image, in the form of a vertical stick that approximates the closest obstacles within a certain vertical slice of the scene.
details: Introduced in 2009, stixels have applications in robotic navigation and advanced driver-assistance systems, where they can be used to define a representation of robotic environments and traffic scenes with a medium level of abstraction.

explainer.lead: A stixel (from "stick" and "pixel") is a superpixel representation of depth information, drawn as a vertical stick approximating the closest obstacles in a vertical slice of the scene. Introduced in 2009, it matters for robotic navigation and driver assistance.

tiers.eli5: Imagine standing up a little stick in each column of a picture to show how close the nearest obstacle is; that stick is a stixel.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use stixels to give robotic environments and traffic scenes a medium-level abstraction for navigation and driver assistance. A pitfall is that each stixel represents only the closest obstacles in its slice, so things behind them are not represented.
tiers.paperLevel: A stixel is a superpixel in the form of a vertical stick approximating the closest obstacles within a vertical slice; its limits follow from the abstraction level, since it captures near obstacles rather than full detail, and it dates from 2009.

explainer.example: A car's vision system divides the road view into vertical slices and marks a stixel in each slice at the nearest obstacle height.
